matches.rationale: Both identify the same issue: the abstract claims training on a much larger dataset (3.5T tokens in ground truth, 1T in finding) and different model sizes than actually used in experiments (Section 3.2.1 describes 400B tokens and 15A2B models). This is the same cross-section inconsistency about experimental scale misreporting.

Both identify contradictory claims about which gating position is most effective. Ground truth notes G1 vs G3 contradiction; finding 12 identifies the text claiming G3 is superior while Table 1 shows G3 performs worse than baseline, directly capturing the method logic inconsistency.

Ground truth concerns overstated claims about training stability at higher learning rates not fully supported by Table 2 and loss plots. While finding 9 mentions hyperparameter tuning issues, it does not address the exaggerated stability claims or cross-reference with loss spike data.

Both address issues with Table 1 data integrity. Ground truth states gating variants show worse or nearly identical performance contradicting improvement claims; finding 13 identifies that PPL values in Table 1 don't support the claimed superiority of certain gating positions, capturing the same evidence corruption.
Ground truth specifically concerns fabricated references [80], [81], [82] in Related Work section. None of the findings identify fake citations or reference fabrication issues.
Ground truth concerns removal of ethical impacts/limitations discussion from Appendix A.5. No findings address missing ethical considerations or broader impacts sections.

Both identify exaggerated claims about attention sink elimination. Ground truth notes abstract claims 'completely eliminates' without qualification; finding 6 identifies the title claims 'Attention-Sink-Free' while the paper acknowledges attention sinks persist, capturing the same rhetorical overstatement.

Both identify cross-section inconsistency about learning rate tolerance. Ground truth notes abstract claims gating 'tolerates larger learning rates' but experiments show divergence; finding 9 identifies contradictory statements about hyperparameter tuning and learning rate benefits in Section 3.2.2 and Table 2.

Both concern experimental design bias in hyperparameter reporting. Ground truth states optimized hyperparameters reported only for baseline with suboptimal configs for gating; finding 8 identifies unclear FFN width reduction specifications making parameter matching verification difficult, capturing similar experimental protocol issues.

Ground truth specifically concerns references [6] and [20] being arXiv preprints from 2025 or unrelated papers. While findings mention various inconsistencies, none specifically identify anachronistic or fabricated references in the bibliography.

Ground truth notes claims of complete elimination of attention sinks contradicted by figures/tables showing partial reduction. Finding 6 identifies the same issue with 'Attention-Sink-Free' title vs. acknowledgment of persistence; finding 15 identifies contradictions in the sparsity-attention sink relationship claims.

Ground truth concerns omission of divergence/instability instances at larger learning rates in Table 2 discussion. While finding 9 mentions hyperparameter issues, it doesn't specifically identify unreported divergence or selective positive result reporting.

Both identify ambiguity in the gating formula definition. Ground truth notes altered formula using additive vs multiplicative gating; finding 4 identifies that Equation (5) and footnote 1 don't clearly specify which hidden states X represents for different gating positions, capturing the same method logic inconsistency.

Both concern altered gating score distributions showing less sparsity than claimed. Ground truth notes Figure 3/Appendix A.6 distributions altered with upward-shifted means; finding 11 identifies Table 4 data contradicting the claimed relationship between gating score sparsity and massive activation reduction.

Both identify cross-section inconsistency where conclusion claims gating 'eliminates attention sinks' but appendix/other sections show residual sinks. Finding 6 captures this by noting the title's 'Attention-Sink-Free' claim contradicts Section 4.3's acknowledgment that attention sinks persist.

Ground truth concerns omission of negative/neutral outcomes for head-shared gating variants, misleading about head-specific gating importance. While finding 15 mentions head-shared gating, it focuses on sparsity-attention sink contradictions, not unreported negative results.
